films.title: Daisies
films.logline: After weeks secretly watching the beautiful but peculiar sisters who live across the street, Oliver and Thomas decide it’s time to make an introduction.

films.title: The Taste of Things
films.logline: Juliette Binoche is divine as a witty 19th-century chef in director Trần Anh Hùng’s Cannes prizewinner, a sumptuous and impossibly romantic tribute to love, food, and joie de vivre.

films.title: Inshallah A Boy
films.logline: After her husband’s death, Nawal faces the loss of her home in this suspenseful and devastating look at a woman driven to extremes. As her brother-in-law claims ownership of the home due to patriarchal marital laws, Nawal constructs a complex web of secrets and lies to buy some time.

films.title: Perfect Days
films.logline: In Wim Wenders’ poetic new film we meet a contented middle-aged Tokyo toilet cleaner whose deep passion for music, books, and photography enriches his structured life.

films.title: ACTIVE CINEMA HIKE
films.logline: Come and enjoy some fresh air and fresh ideas with filmmakers, friends, festival staff and cinephiles during this hour-long hike to the ocean through beautiful terrain.

films.title: Bloody river
films.logline: A moment of ice-cold horror.

films.title: Once Was
films.logline: A woman's reunion with a romantic partner spurs a moment of reflection.

films.title: Heartbeat
films.logline: In Mexico City, Leonor wants a baby but can’t conceive while 16-year-old Emilia is reluctantly pregnant. The solution seems simple but reality is more complicated. Director Katina Medina Mora’s sensitive film deftly portrays two women negotiating the complexities of intimacy.

films.title: From The Shadow Of A Mountain
films.logline: Markelle Taylor runs the Dipsea, America’s oldest trail race.

films.title: Carol Doda Topless at the Condor
films.logline: San Francisco’s first topless dancer, the legendary Carol Doda, reshaped the city’s nightlife and transformed America’s relationship to female nudity in the 1960s. This fascinating documentary explores the legacy of a game-changing icon.

films.title: Light Beams For Helena
films.logline: Director Kirk Horton’s film explores a woman’s journey with depression, her ongoing mental health efforts, and what diving into the darkness of deep water has taught her about life and light.

films.title: The Persian Version
films.logline: Mother-daughter conflicts have rarely been depicted with such deftness and wit as in Maryam Keshavarz’s exuberant and genre-busting film about a queer aspiring filmmaker who dreams of being the “Iranian-American Scorsese."

films.title: Shorts: The Circle Game
films.logline: Themes of memory, legacy, and family unify this stirring collection of shorts.

films.title: Masterclass: On Filmmaking with Chloe Domont
films.logline: In this conversation, Chloe Domont unpacks the creative process behind her work, including development from script to screen, and the challenges of making a feature in the current market.

films.title: Housekeeping for Beginners
films.logline: Goran Stolevski’s third feature centers on an unconventional family of Roma LGBTQ friends. When one is diagnosed with cancer, the community steps up to parent her daughters and her partner marries a gay man to form a nuclear family. Bighearted, funny, and tough, the drama is a brash ode to love and resilience.

films.title: Saltburn
films.logline: Oscar® winner Emerald Fennell ( Promising Young Woman , MVFF43) proves herself a bright star of new British cinema with this wickedly funny mix of revenge comedy and erotic thriller starring Barry Keoghan ( The Banshees of Inisherin , MVFF45).

films.title: The 9 Lives of Barbara Dane • Performances with Special Guests including Holly Near and Willie Chambers
films.logline: A special one-of-a-kind tribute concert honoring the legendary Barbara Dane and the much-anticipated premiere of Maureen Gosling's captivating documentary, The 9 Lives of Barbara Dane .

films.title: The 9 Lives of Barbara Dane
films.logline: Maureen Gosling celebrates the life of singer Barbara Dane, a woman whose stellar voice supported justice movements in the Bay Area and beyond for decades, garnering an impressive FBI file along the way.

films.title: Bestiary
films.logline: A trio of mean girls chooses a new target for their vicious bullying, sparking intense rivalries and violent impulses that threaten to spin out of control.

films.title: Operation Frankenstein
films.logline: Three mischievous siblings discover part of a mannequin in a dumpster and see it as a perfect opportunity to build their very own Frankenstein monster.

films.title: Keynote: The Time Is Now: Building a New Film Ecosystem with Ted Hope
films.logline: Ted Hope will explain why the conditions are right for a total reboot of cinema and how we can all offer a hand, using all that we really know but somehow forgot or never properly respected.

films.title: Adrift
films.logline: Veteran filmmaker Rory Kennedy launches a welcome intervention into the ongoing global refugee crisis.

films.title: Panel: AI: Perils, Possibilities, Promises
films.logline: With this moderated conversation, our participants offer a diversity of perspectives on the ethics and creative potential of AI in film and media productions.

films.title: David's Doodles
films.logline: An autistic teenage cartoonist shares his work, his creative process, and his greatest weakness: drawing realistically.

films.title: Nyad
films.logline: The extraordinary true story of long-distance swimmer Diana Nyad’s (Annette Bening) attempt to swim from Cuba to Florida at the age of 64, with the support of her coach and longtime friend Bonnie Stoll (Jodie Foster).

films.title: Periodical
films.logline: With Gloria Steinem, Megan Rapinoe, and Naomi Watts adding star power, this eye-opening documentary explores the fascinating science, politics, and mystery of the menstrual cycle.

films.title: Música!
films.logline: Venerated Bay Area documentarians Rob Epstein and Jeffrey Friedman’s latest celebrates a unique partnership between US and Cuban musicians, as well as the rich sonic traditions and budding young performers it helps sustain.

films.title: Frybread Face and Me
films.logline: Produced by Taika Waititi, director Billy Luther’s tender and wistfully funny debut spins the coming-of-age tale of two Navajo cousins spending the summer of 1990 together at their grandmother’s reservation home.

films.title: Circle of Donuts
films.logline: Here we meet a Japanese immigrant who traveled across the world at a young age and paved a unique path to success.

films.title: binary.
films.logline: In this intimate look into the life of a young transgender person inspired by androgynous rockstars, a teen struggles to understand who they really are while facing conflict with those around them.

films.title: Farming While Black
films.logline: Mark Decena’s visually eloquent documentary celebrates the rich heritage of Black farmers through the experiences of three people who make their living off the land.

films.title: An Evening of East and West Coast Renegade Radio featuring Taj Mahal and Jesse Colin Young
films.logline: Following the California premiere of Jay Schlossberg’s documentary feature film Feast Your Ears: The Story of WHFS 102.3 , we're turning up the heat with a live concert celebrating iconic independent radio stations.

films.title: New Moon
films.logline: Young Jay Jay and his mother Edie embark on a magical journey to rediscover lost dreams and nurture new hopes.

films.title: Swimming The Rock
films.logline: A man overcomes his grief by swimming to shore from Alcatraz.

films.title: Shorts: ¡Viva el cine infantil!
films.logline: As part of MVFF’s ¡Viva el cine! programming, we invite families and younger viewers to join our annual celebration of Spanish-language and Latinx films with this festive collection of kid-centric animated and narrative shorts. Ages 6+

films.title: Telephone
films.logline: Activist screendance documentary celebrating audio description for dance which allows blind and visually impaired people to be included fully in the joy of artistic expression.

films.title: Evil Does Not Exist
films.logline: Oscar® winner Ryûsuke Hamaguchi ( Drive My Car , MVFF44) builds his beautifully evocative and unequivocally political film around the most pressing issues of our time: corporate greed vs. environmental protection, and centralized power vs. community control.

films.title: I Am Hope
films.logline: Through fascinating fly-on-the-wall footage and insightful interviews, director ShakaJamal chronicles the effort to create a yoga and mindfulness program for Oakland middle schools.

films.title: Between Earth & Sky
films.logline: Renowned ecologist Nalini Nadkarni must turn her research onto herself in order to understand the effects of disturbance and recovery throughout her life.

films.title: Companion
films.logline: A woman faces the reality that maybe her roommate needs different things in their relationship.

films.title: For Her
films.logline: An Iranian youth finds fierce loyalty and solidarity among her two closest friends.

films.title: MIND THE GAP SUMMIT
films.logline: Join us as we celebrate the incredible work of female filmmakers, nonbinary filmmakers, trans filmmakers, and other marginalized filmmakers from around the world.

films.title: Burnout
films.logline: A clever mix of animation, music, and poetic narration illustrates the childlike creativity that fuels our ideas, and how quickly that can sour if expended in large bursts too fast.

films.title: With a Wool Ball
films.logline: In this stop-motion animation made from wool, a girl from the northwestern hills of Argentina spends the cold winters in a hut, knitting ponchos made of wool for her friends, the native animals that live around her.

films.title: If Only I Could Hibernate
films.logline: With warmth and empathy, this sensitive debut tells the moving story of a teenage physics prodigy juggling familial and academic responsibilities in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.

films.title: Mountain Man
films.logline: In this sharp animation, a mountain man battles an antagonist made of stone amidst a harsh winter landscape. Good thing he’s a skilled skier.

films.title: Shorts: Monsters, Movies & the Moon
films.logline: Take a wild ride from Oakland to Zimbabwe in this fun and fanciful collection of stories filled with crazy monsters, classic movies, and enchanting trips to the moon.

films.title: Goodbye Julia
films.logline: In this powerful drama set against the 2011 split of Sudan, a fragile friendship develops between two women despite differences in religion and social standing. However, there are buried deceptions at play.

films.title: Patrol
films.logline: Illegal cattle ranching poses an existential threat to one of the most biodiverse regions in Central America. This stirring documentary follows the Rama-Kriol peoples' efforts to save this precious ecosystem before it’s too late.

films.title: The Piñata
films.logline: Seven-year-old Lorena is determined to win the school's piñata contest and its coveted grand prize: a new bicycle.

films.title: FILMMAKER PARTY • COMMUNITY MIXER
films.logline: Join us for an exciting gathering of filmmakers and film lovers from the Bay Area and beyond!

films.title: La Chimera
films.logline: From Alice Rohrwacher ( Le Pupille , MVFF45), a marvelous fantasy-comedy on the themes of love, loss, and Etruscan antiquities set in 1980s Tuscany, with The Crown 's Josh O’Connor terrific as an archaeological scholar-turned-artifact robber.

films.title: Another Body
films.logline: Some guys take rejection and compose beautiful love songs; others make deepfake revenge porn. Turns out both are perfectly legal and potentially profitable. In this eye-opening doc, a woman seeks justice.

films.title: Under the Same Sky
films.logline: Andrea and Marina become fast friends while playing on the rooftops of their adjacent buildings during the pandemic in Mexico City.

films.title: Farther
films.logline: A father faces some difficult truths when he revisits the past with his daughter.

films.title: Totem
films.logline: Lila Avilés’ impressionistic drama observes the intimacies of a sprawling middle-class family in crisis through the eyes of a child.

films.title: Society of the Snow
films.logline: Based on Pablo Vierci’s book about the astonishing true story of the 1972 Uruguayan Andes air disaster, this gripping thriller from J.A. Bayona relates the survivors’ struggle to endure for 72 days without food or shelter.

films.title: The Boy and the Heron
films.original_title: 君たちはどう生きるか
films.logline: Legendary director Hayao Miyazaki’s new animated spectacular is another dizzying fantasy adventure as a Japanese boy, haunted by his past, discovers a strange alternate universe and the role he must play there.

films.title: La Calesita
films.logline: An animated tribute to the beloved Argentinian merry-go-round operators who have dedicated their lives to providing fun and happiness to children and their communities.

films.title: The Right To Read
films.logline: Executive produced by LeVar Burton, Jenny Mackenzie’s inspiring doc introduces us to several Bay Area residents taking action to reverse the disturbing trend of plummeting literacy — and give our children a brighter future full of appreciation for the written word.

films.title: The Nature of Love
films.logline: Sophia, 40, is lively, erudite, and bored. When sent by her long-time partner to supervise renovations at their country chalet, she meets Sylvain, and their erotic coup de foudre threatens to scorch all within range.

films.title: Maestro
films.logline: Bradley Cooper and Carey Mulligan deliver stunning performances as Leonard Bernstein and his wife, actress Felicia Montealegre, in this intimate dramatic portrait of their marriage and a career that made him an indispensable figure in the history of classical music. Along with his extraordinary portrayal, Cooper directs and co-wrote the script.

films.title: PASSING SPACESHIPS: AN EARTHLY CONVERSATION WITH BOOTS RILEY AND SEPHORA WOLDU
films.logline: Join us for a casual gathering with Boots and Sephora on unorthodox storytelling, indie filmmaking, and how fellow filmmakers can be your north star.

films.title: Sirocco and the Kingdom of the Winds
films.original_title: Sirocco et le royaume des courants d'air
films.logline: Kids become kitties in this surreal yet serene animated French tale of two little girls stuck in the fantasy world of their favorite children’s books.

films.title: Weirdos
films.logline: Could Jasmine and her middle-school frenemies be humanity’s best chance at stopping a monster invasion?

films.title: The Teachers' Lounge
films.logline: This gripping drama examines racism and institutional bureaucracy, putting you through an emotional and moral wringer as a well-meaning middle-school teacher makes a split-second decision that brings her idealism crashing down.

films.title: For the Skeptical
films.logline: Filmmaker Dawn Westlake asks us to stop autocracy in its tracks, with facts. Because despite the cultural and economic shifts, one thing will always matter: the truth.

films.title: El Moño
films.logline: After her favorite sock goes missing, Andrea learns some family magic that helps her find lost objects in the most unexpected way.

films.title: My Sisters In The Stars: The Story of Lee Yong-soo
films.logline: This powerful documentary chronicles the painful history and current activism of a former Korean “comfort woman” who was abducted at age 14 by the Japanese Army during WWII and forced into sexual slavery.

films.title: Invisible Nation
films.logline: Vanessa Hope’s arresting documentary examines Taiwan’s — and democracy’s — urgent fight for survival.

films.title: Clownin'
films.logline: It’s hard out there for a clown—and even harder for those aspiring to become one.

films.title: One With The Whale
films.logline: Modern technology confronts ancient ritual in this profound and heartwarming documentary about a Siberian Yupik community's way of life.

films.title: The Crime is Mine
films.logline: In 1930s Paris, two young women become embroiled in a murder case, turning its scandalous headlines to their mutual advantage. Director François Ozon’s latest is an ode to vintage screwball comedy, with an extravagantly outrageous Isabelle Huppert.

films.title: The Bikeriders
films.logline: Anchored by phenomenal performances from Jodie Comer, Tom Hardy, and Austin Butler, this latest from indie auteur Jeff Nichols ( Loving , MVFF39) chronicles a fictional biker gang in the mid-’60s Chicago.

films.title: The Disappearance of Shere Hite
films.logline: This beautifully crafted documentary profiles sexologist Shere Hite, a hardworking history student destined to make history, who revolutionized the cultural conversation about sex.

films.title: The Hypnosis
films.logline: An aspiring entrepreneur and his girlfriend attend a seminar to pitch their new app, not realizing her recent hypnotherapy has severed her inhibitions. An excruciatingly funny cringe comedy, it’s also a touching love story about truly seeing your partner for the first time.

films.title: Demon Mineral
films.logline: Hadley Austin’s fascinating documentary offers a penetrating look at the effects of radiation poisoning on Navajo land after decades of uranium mining.

films.title: Common Ground
films.logline: This dramatic doc focuses on the power of regenerative agriculture to transform the Earth, and how innovative farmers are developing strategies to revive our faltering ecosystem. With appearances by Laura Dern, Donald Glover, and Rosario Dawson.

films.title: The Hi De Ho Show
films.logline: Our host John Goddard explores the birth of rock’n’roll as he veejays an evening unpacking the marvels and mysteries, backstories and gossip of that mid-20th-century movement that changed the world forever.

films.title: Öte
films.logline: In this quietly beguiling film, a Black American woman traveling solo through Turkey forges unexpected connections as she explores the landscape.

films.title: Fingernails
films.logline: At the “Love Institute,” couples seek to reduce the risks of romance. Director Christos Nikou and a stellar cast (Jessie Buckley, Jeremy Allen White, Riz Ahmed) brilliantly craft a story-world that is both distant from our own yet almost too close for comfort.

films.title: Better late than never
films.logline: In skeletal stop-motion, two cousins at a Day of the Dead celebration impatiently await their Tia Carmen who is late with the food.

films.title: I'm Hip
films.logline: A self-absorbed cat, in a jazzy song and dance, proudly and comically proclaims his “hipness” to the world. The world is less convinced than he is.

films.title: Feast Your Ears: The Story of WHFS 102.3 FM
films.logline: This doc pays loving tribute to the culturally influential Maryland radio station whose progressive format reigned supreme from the '60s to the '80s, offering a vital alternative to Top 40 sameness.

films.title: The Settlers
films.logline: With a refreshingly modern sensibility, haunting cinematography, and an evocative score, Felipe Gálvez’s ambitious and expertly crafted debut charts the depredations visited on Indigenous people of Tierra del Fuego in 1901.

films.title: Founder Girls
films.logline: In this kaleidoscopic ode to girlhood, young campers find freedom, sisterhood, and themselves at a historically Black summer camp.

films.title: National Anthem
films.logline: This open-hearted story about a community of free-spirited queer rodeo performers is a southwestern ranch romance for the 21st century.

films.title: Gaby's Hills
films.logline: Puberty rears its head unexpectedly for one girl as she navigates relationships with male schoolmates.

films.title: Fallen Leaves
films.logline: Finnish writer-director Aki Kaurismäki reasserts himself as the master of the wry, melancholy comedy with this tale of two lonely souls forging a love connection in Helsinki.

films.title: B Word
films.logline: Maternal longings go viral within a woman’s social circle.

films.title: Shadowstalker
films.logline: Outlines the history of Predictive Policing, the dangers of identity theft which targets victims with a bias on race and economics, and the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s use of AI.

films.title: The Pigeon Tunnel
films.logline: Academy Award®-winner Errol Morris’ mesmerizing profile of novelist John le Carré gets personal and profound, revealing how his upbringing forged a great literary facility with the themes of falsehood, betrayal, and spycraft.

films.title: Fancy Dance
films.logline: Elements of the mystery and road movie genres combine in Erica Tremblay’s moving narrative debut, focusing on teenage Roki and her Aunt Jax as they search for Roki’s missing mother.

films.title: Gugu naGogo
films.logline: When a lunar eclipse interferes with their magical late-night letter exchanges, 12-year-old aspiring astronomer Gugu must find a new way to reconnect with her beloved grandmother.

films.title: Panel: State of the Industry
films.logline: In this brave new world, are theatrical distribution and exhibition worth saving? Are streamers really the golden cow the studios thought they'd be? MVFF Executive Director Mark Fishkin invites respected industry veterans to weigh in on pressing issues.

films.title: Skin of Glass
films.logline: When she learns that squatters occupy the now-dilapidated São Paulo skyscraper her late father designed, Bay Area documentarian Denise Zmekhol returns home to investigate – and make peace with her dad.

films.title: Day of the Fight
films.logline: Renowned actor Jack Huston’s extraordinary writing/directing debut is an exquisitely composed, understated portrait of a complicated former boxing champ coming to grips with his past.

films.title: Robot Dreams
films.logline: In a hand-drawn work of melancholy beauty, director Pablo Berger ( Blancanieves ) and Sara Varon adapt her graphic novel about the bond between a lonely canine and a robot in 1980s Manhattan.

films.title: Shorts: Emma Lee
films.logline: Women write and/or direct women-centered stories in this fun assembly of shorts.

films.title: PANEL: Forging Paths: Navigating the U.S. Film Market for Independent Latin American Filmmakers
films.logline: Navigating the U.S. Film Market for Independent Latin American Filmmakers

films.title: A Double Life
films.logline: Filled with the radical political fervor of his times, lawyer Stephen Bingham’s devotion to prison reform came at a high price.

films.title: Anatomy of a Fall
films.logline: French director Justine Triet’s gripping procedural mixes marriage story and courtroom drama, with Sandra Hüller as an enigmatic writer whose husband (Swann Arlaud) died — either by suicide or murder.

films.title: An Ordinary Day
films.logline: Two female friends — one blind, the other in a wheelchair — find that time they decided to spend together is anything but ordinary.

films.title: How To Live 100 Years (or more)
films.logline: A contemplation of longevity. A wordless video essay. A cinematic collaboration between documentary film maker Gary Weimberg (2-time Emmy award winner, 6-time Emmy nominee) and sound designer Gary Rydstrom (7-time Oscar winner, 20-time nominee).

films.title: Logic Paralyzes the Heart
films.logline: This is the story of the first cyborg, portrayed by actress Joan Chen, who details the history of cyborgian technology from its early intention as a tool for human liberation to the break between ethical human advancement and exploitation.

films.title: Panel: Accessibility in Exhibition: Take Action with Resources
films.logline: Join Cassidy Dimon (Director of Programs, Events & Accessibility - Full Spectrum Features and FEAW (Film Event Accessibility Working Group)) in a pre-recorded discussion regarding the resources one can find and utilize to create accessible event spaces and engage with our disabled communities.

films.title: Shorts: You Got to Run
films.logline: Kindred spirits find joy, comfort, and support in these short films that celebrate friendships, both new and seasoned, in lovely detail.

films.title: Mountains
films.logline: Monica Sorelle’s breathtaking first feature unfolds as a hypnotic slow burn of one family’s struggles, focusing on a Haitian demolition worker watching the gentrification of his Miami neighborhood.

films.title: Take Me Home
films.logline: Two sisters to confront the reality of a major change in their lives.

films.title: Rustin
films.logline: Colman Domingo’s ( If Beale Street Could Talk, MVFF41) fully inhabits this rousing and intimate portrait of gay Civil Rights leader Bayard Rustin, focused on his activism in the weeks leading up to the historic 1963 March on Washington.

films.title: Room
films.logline: Struggling with depression and social anxiety, a teen locks himself in his imaginary room as his life plays out around him. Told through remarkable miniatures, the film follows his post-pandemic journey as he tries to escape from his psychological lockdown.

films.title: Terrestrial Verses
films.logline: Spare, vivid, and, above all, humane, this series of satirical vignettes set in Tehran depicts the quiet courage it takes to negotiate the everyday absurdities of totalitarianism.

films.title: Shorts: Youth Works
films.logline: This year’s collection of peer-reviewed, youth-produced short films presents an inspiring display of emerging young talent from as close to home as San Rafael and San Francisco and as far afield as Australia, Belgium, and Belarus.

films.title: Summer Solstice
films.logline: Bobbi Salvör Menuez is luminous as Leo, a young trans man weekending in the countryside with Eleanor, his cis straight crush from college. Their seemingly carefree youth collides with the realities of adulting, forcing big questions.

films.title: Avenue of the Giants
films.logline: Bay Area filmmaker Finn Taylor movingly dramatizes the true story of Auschwitz survivor Herbert Heller (Stephen Lang), who kept his past a secret for more than 50 years — until the unexpected friendship of a troubled teenager (Elsie Fisher) made hope and healing possible.

films.title: No More Longing
films.logline: From Brazil to California and four years after starting testosterone, Jaime Jobim searches for his new voice.

films.title: Cleo & Nina
films.logline: This animated documentary brings to life a phone call between five-year-old Sara and her grandmother Nina with a story about Nina’s childhood pet pig and an itchy dress.

films.title: Seaweed
films.logline: A chance encounter between an Israeli boy and a mysterious stranger yields something special.

films.title: A Life in Technicolor
films.logline: Alone in her apartment during the pandemic, Natalie turns to her favorite classic movies to keep her company.

films.title: The Promised Land
films.logline: It’s 1755 and Captain Ludvig Kahlen (Mads Mikkelsen) seeks to establish a settlement in the name of the Danish King. His sole reward: a royal title for himself. Mikkelsen has never been “Madder” than in this sweepingly cinematic must-see modern classic.

films.title: Eat Flowers
films.logline: When photographer and writer Cig Harvey discovers her best friend has leukemia, she sets out to fill her world with color and light.

films.title: Water For Life
films.logline: Documentarian Will Parrinello gets astonishingly close as he captures the efforts of three environmental defenders in Chile, El Salvador, and Honduras, all fighting for clean water.

films.title: Immortality
films.logline: Written and performed by a Cyborg – a GPT-3 Chatbot, considers how to transform human discrimination and technological weapons into tools of survival.

films.title: Place Setting
films.logline: An immersion into the exquisite tactility of housekeeping finds expression and rebellion.

films.title: The Lake Merritt Monster
films.logline: When Ollie’s mother is attacked by a monster hiding in the depths of Lake Merritt, he sets out on a mission to find her—discovering instead a hidden network of monster-hunters tasked with protecting Oakland from its own dark underbelly.

films.title: Mustache
films.logline: With a solid ensemble including Alicia Silverstone, Hasan Minhaj, and Rizwan Manji, this heartfelt comedy offers a look at the Pakistani-American immigrant experience in 1990s Silicon Valley.

films.title: American Fiction
films.logline: Writer Cord Jefferson ( The Good Place ) proves himself a director to watch with this impressive adaptation of Percival Everett’s Erasure , starring Jeffrey Wright.

films.title: Pripyat Horse
films.logline: Sally Patrica Pearce shares a moment of mourning — for a friend, and for the Earth.

films.title: Cyborgian Rhapsody
films.logline: A long fascination with AI—its potentials, uses, and abuses—is at the heart of visionary San Francisco artist and filmmaker Lynn Hershman Leeson’s four short films under the collective title Cyborgian Rhapsody , featuring performances by Tessa Thompson ( Passing , MVFF44) and Joan Chen ( Lust, Caution , MVFF32).

films.title: Tracing History
films.logline: A Chinese-American filmmaker and her mother contemplate loss and legacy while visiting sites where their Chinese ancestors labored.

films.title: Starling
films.logline: A heavenly body finds itself on an Earth-bound trajectory.

films.title: Seduction of a Cyborg
films.logline: A poetic metaphor about the invasion of technology into an unsuspecting body, causing vision loss.

films.title: Milli Vanilli
films.logline: This deep-dive documentary corrects the record on the sensational ’80s pop duo done in by a rapacious music industry.

films.title: Mist
films.logline: When Nicolas and his family move from the city to a new house next to a forest, his perception starts to change thanks to mysterious encounters with native animals.

films.title: The Lampboy, or The Universe Between Us
films.original_title: Der Lampenjunge, oder Das Universum zwischen uns
films.logline: A woman experiences a sexual reawakening when she finds herself in a surprise hookup.

films.title: A Conversation in Passing
films.logline: Two strangers find themselves in a surreal chat.

films.title: Chasin' Butterflies
films.logline: Filmmakers Joshua Harding, Adam Hobbs, and Matt Klug introduce us to an unforgettable, eccentric, playful, provocative, self-taught artist from rural Alabama.

films.title: Priscilla
films.logline: Director Sofia Coppola’s exquisite gift for depicting the complex psychology of young women is in ample evidence in this superb star-crossed love story. Based on Priscilla Presley’s best-selling memoir.

films.title: Goose Town
films.logline: An urban teenager finds solace from his chaotic home life in a fictional cowboy outlaw persona, but risks taking the cosplay one step too far.

films.title: Masterclass: On Animation with John Musker
films.logline: Join legendary animator, screenwriter, director, and producer John Musker ( Aladdin , The Little Mermaid , Moana )_ _as he gives an inside look into the process of his newest venture, the independently made short, I'm Hip .

films.title: Radical
films.logline: This audience favorite from Sundance 2023 dramatizes how a schoolteacher in Mexico threw out the rule book so his sixth-graders could see their true potential.

films.title: Kidnapped
films.logline: Marco Bellocchio’s historical drama portrays the true story of Edgardo Mortara, a Jewish boy baptized in 1857 Bologna and taken from his family by the Papal States.

films.title: The Innocent Bystander
films.logline: Sally Eckhoff's animation pays affectionate tribute to the late San Francisco musician Dan Hicks.

films.title: They Shot the Piano Player
films.logline: A New York music journalist (voiced by Jeff Goldblum) investigates the 1976 disappearance of Brazilian piano virtuoso Francisco Tenório Júnior. The sounds of bossa nova, delivered by the era’s musical luminaries, bring Tenório's intriguing story to vivid life.

films.title: Dance With Me
films.logline: Imagine putting on a blindfold on a busy Berkeley street corner and inviting strangers to dance with you. That’s what Gabriel Diamond did.

films.title: The Fortunate Ones
films.logline: Surprises are afoot in Swiss director Jeanne Waltz’s flavorful drama set in Portugal’s southernmost Algarve region, where an impulsive young woman scandalizes her neglectful wealthy family with an interracial romance.

films.title: Gone Before Your Eyes
films.logline: An artist finds herself in a disorienting painting session.

films.title: Strawberry Picker
films.logline: San Francisco printmaker and social activist Juan R. Fuentes reflects on generations of struggle and resilience in the Chicano art community.

films.title: The Dance
films.logline: Andrés gets invited to the school dance by the girl he likes, but there's one problem: His shoe has a hole in it. With only a day left, Andrés must find a way to fix his shoe and impress his crush.

films.title: Education Workshop: Mindfulness in the Classroom
films.logline: FOLLOWING THE FRIDAY, OCT. 13 SCREENING: W. Kamau Bell in conversation with Ericka Huggins and ShakaJamal.

films.title: Panel: Balancing Act: Virtual Production Technology in the Creative Process
films.logline: Whether you're a director, producer, or a curious cinephile, this panel encourages thoughtful consideration of VP's role in enhancing a narrative story. Join us for a practical journey into VP's world of possibilities.

films.title: Shorts: It's My Way
films.logline: This documentary shorts program with strong Bay Area ties follows exceptional individuals bravely delving into their roots.

films.title: All Happy Families
films.logline: A deeply relatable portrait of family dysfunction in which two competitive brothers reunite in their childhood home for one eventful weekend, revealing secrets and airing out long-held resentments.

films.title: May December
films.logline: A battle of wills develops between an actress (Natalie Portman) and the controversial woman (Julianne Moore) she’s been hired to portray. Under the keen eye of director Todd Haynes (Tribute, MVFF40), family secrets are revealed, surprise motivations surfaced, and our expectations upended.

films.title: River of Desire
films.logline: Lushly set in the Brazilian Amazon, acclaimed writer-director Sérgio Machado’s sultry drama follows three brothers entangled in a thorny co-habitation with the middle sibling’s new wife.

films.title: Yesterday, Again
films.logline: In CG animation, a former pilot reflects on his past and how his memories shape his choices.

films.title: Monster
films.logline: This Rashomon -like drama explores a troubling school incident from multiple perspectives. Shoplifters (MVFF41) director Hirokazu Kore-eda presents a study of bullying and youthful yearning, showing how confusing life can be to both adults and children.

films.title: Shorts: Eventually
films.logline: In this shorts program, we present a collection of true-life tales about extraordinary individuals from around the world.

films.title: The Holdovers
films.logline: Alexander Payne’s moving and funny latest is set in 1971 at an elite boarding school, where curmudgeonly Professor Hunham (a terrific Paul Giamatti) has the responsibility of staying on campus over winter break to supervise those few kids unable to go home for the holidays.

films.title: Rosa and the Stone Troll
films.logline: Rosa, a timid flower fairy, befriends Silk, a fearless butterfly. When a Stone Troll kidnaps Silk, Rosa must find the courage to save her. With friendship as her guiding light, Rosa learns to open her heart.

films.title: The Zone of Interest
films.logline: Adapting the Martin Amis novel, Under the Skin filmmaker Jonathan Glazer finds a startling new way to depict the Holocaust: through the blinkered perspective of the monsters who orchestrated it.

films.title: Fast Charlie
films.logline: The Deep South gets hot indeed as veteran hitman Pierce Brosnan finds himself in the middle of an organized-crime turf war. This backroads noir provides a rogue’s gallery of colorful figures including James Caan in one of his final roles.
